sentences.translation: جلس السيد ألكسندر بونابرت كاست دون حركة. كان فطوره بارداً ولم يمسه على طبقه. كان يقرأ صحيفة باهتمام كبير.

sentences.text: Suddenly he got up, walked up and down for a minute, then sat down again on a chair by the window.
sentences.translation: فجأة نهض، سار ذهاباً وإياباً لدقيقة، ثم جلس مرة أخرى على كرسي بجانب النافذة.

sentences.text: He rested his head in his hands. He didn't hear the sound of the opening door. Mrs Marbury, the owner of the building, stood in the doorway.
sentences.translation: أراح رأسه في يديه. لم يسمع صوت فتح الباب. وقفت السيدة ماربوري، مالكة المبنى، في المدخل.

sentences.text: 'What's the matter, Mr Cust? You haven't touched your breakfast. Is your head hurting you again?'
'No. I mean, yes... I just feel a little unwell.'
'Well, I'm sorry. You aren't going to go away today, then?'
Mr Cust jumped up quickly. 'No, no, I have to go. It's business. Very important business.'
sentences.translation: قفز السيد كاست بسرعة.

sentences.text: His hands were shaking. 'I'm going to - Cheltenham.'
sentences.translation: كانت يداه ترتجفان.

sentences.text: He said the word so strangely that Mrs Marbury looked at him in surprise.
sentences.translation: قال الكلمة بغرابة شديدة لدرجة أن السيدة ماربوري نظرت إليه بدهشة.

sentences.text: 'Cheltenham's a nice place,' she said conversationally. She bent down and picked up the newspaper, which was lying on the floor.
sentences.translation: قالت بمحادثة. انحنت والتقطت الصحيفة التي كانت ملقاة على الأرض.

sentences.text: 'The newspapers are full of these murders,' she said. 'Doncaster - that's the place he's going to carry out his next murder. And tomorrow!'
sentences.translation: قالت.

sentences.text: It's the races, too. They say that hundreds of police are being brought in - Mr Cust, you do look bad. Really, you oughtn't to go travelling today.'
sentences.translation: إنه سباق الخيل أيضاً. يقولون إن مئات من الشرطة يتم استدعاؤهم - سيد كاست، تبدو بحالة سيئة حقاً. حقاً، لا يجب أن تسافر اليوم.

sentences.text: 'It's necessary, Mrs Marbury. When I've promised to do something, I always do it. It's the only way to succeed in in - business.'
'But if you're ill?'
'I'm not ill, Mrs Marbury. Just a little worried about - personal matters. I slept badly.'
'I'm really quite all right.'
Mrs Marbury picked up the breakfast things and left the room. Mr Cust took out a suitcase and packed some clothes.
sentences.translation: التقطت السيدة ماربوري أدوات الفطور وغادرت الغرفة. أخرج السيد كاست حقيبة وحزم بعض الملابس.

sentences.text: Then he unlocked a cupboard. He took out about twelve flat boxes and put them in the suitcase, too.
sentences.translation: ثم فتح خزانة. أخرج حوالي اثني عشر صندوقاً مسطحاً ووضعها في الحقيبة أيضاً.

sentences.text: Lily, Mrs Marbury's daughter, came out of another room.
sentences.translation: خرجت ليلي، ابنة السيدة ماربوري، من غرفة أخرى.

sentences.text: 'Where are you going this time, Mr Cust?,' she said. 'To the seaside again?'
sentences.translation: قالت.

sentences.text: 'No, no - er - Cheltenham.'
'Well, that's nice, too. But not quite as nice as Torquay. I want to go there for my holiday next year.'
You were probably quite near where the murder was - the ABC murder. It happened when you were down there, didn't it?'
sentences.translation: كنت على الأرجح قريباً جداً من مكان الجريمة - جريمة ABC. حدثت عندما كنت هناك، أليس كذلك؟

sentences.text: 'Er - yes. But Churston's ten or eleven kilometres away.'
'How exciting. Perhaps you passed the murderer on the street!'
'Yes, perhaps,' said Mr Cust. He smiled a strange smile.
sentences.translation: قال السيد كاست. ابتسم ابتسامة غريبة.

sentences.text: 'Oh, Mr Cust, you don't look well,' said Lily.
sentences.translation: قالت ليلي.

sentences.text: 'I'm quite all right, quite all right. Goodbye, Miss Marbury.'
He picked up his suitcase and hurried out of the front door.
sentences.translation: رفع حقيبته وأسرع خارجاً من الباب الأمامي.

sentences.text: 'Funny old thing,' said Lily Marbury to herself. 'He looks half mad.'
sentences.translation: قالت ليلي ماربوري لنفسها.

sentences.text: Inspector Crome said to his assistant, 'Get me a list of all the companies who make stockings. And I want a list of all their agents who go to people's houses selling the stockings.'
sentences.translation: قال المفتش كروم لمساعده:

sentences.text: 'Is this for the ABC case, sir?' asked the assistant.
sentences.translation: سأل المساعد.

sentences.text: 'Yes. One of Hercule Poirot's ideas.' The Inspector's voice was not very enthusiastic.
sentences.translation: لم يكن صوت المفتش متحمساً جداً.

sentences.text: 'Right, sir, Mr Poirot's done some good work in the past, but I think he's a bit old now, sir.'
'He loves to get attention,' said the Inspector. 'But he's not as clever as he wants people to think.'
sentences.translation: قال المفتش.

sentences.text: Now, the arrangements for Doncaster...'
sentences.translation: الآن، الترتيبات لدونكاستر...

sentences.text: Lily Marbury was dancing with her boyfriend, Tom Hartigan. As they danced, they talked.
'I saw old Mr Cust this morning,' said Tom. At Euston Station. He was looking lost, as usual.
sentences.translation: قال توم. في محطة يوستون. كان يبدو تائهاً، كالمعتاد.

sentences.text: First he dropped his paper and then he dropped his ticket. I picked it up. He thanked me, but I don't think he recognised me.'
sentences.translation: أسقط صحيفته أولاً ثم أسقط تذكرته. التقطتها له. شكرني، لكنني لا أعتقد أنه تعرف عليّ.

sentences.text: 'Did you say Euston or Paddington?' asked Lily.
sentences.translation: سألت ليلي.

sentences.text: 'Euston.'
'That's strange. I thought trains went to Cheltenham from Paddington.'
'That's right. But old Cust wasn't going to Cheltenham. He was going to Doncaster. I saw his ticket.'
'Well, he told me he was going to Cheltenham. I'm sure he did.'
'No - you're wrong. He was going to Doncaster.'
'Oh, Tom, I hope he won't get murdered. Doncaster is where the ABC murder is going to happen.'
'Cust will be all right. His name doesn't begin with a D.'
'He was down near Churston at Torquay when the last murder happened.'
'Was he? That's a coincident, isn't it?' Tom laughed. 'He wasn't at Bexhill before that, was he?'
sentences.translation: ضحك توم.

sentences.text: 'He was away... Yes, I remember he was away,' said Lily, 'because he forgot his swimsuit. Mother was mending it for him.'
sentences.translation: قالت ليلي،

sentences.text: 'Well, if he wanted his swimsuit, he was at the seaside. Lily,' said Tom with an amused look, 'perhaps old Mr Cust is the murderer!'
sentences.translation: قال توم بنظرة مستمتعة،

sentences.text: 'Mr Cust wouldn't hurt anything or anyone,' laughed Lily.
sentences.translation: ضحكت ليلي.

sentences.text: They continued to dance.
sentences.translation: واصلا الرقص.

sentences.text: Doncaster!
sentences.translation: دونكاستر!

sentences.text: I shall, I think, remember 11 September all my life. We were all there, at the St Leger - Poirot, myself, Clarke, Fraser, Megan Barnard, Thora Grey and Mary Drower.
sentences.translation: سأتذكر، كما أعتقد، الحادي عشر من سبتمبر طوال حياتي. كنا جميعاً هناك، في سباق سانت ليجيه - بوارو، وأنا، وكلارك، وفريزر، وميغان بارنارد، وثورا غراي، وماري دراور.

sentences.text: But what could any of us do? Thora Grey was the only person who might be able to recognise the murderer.
sentences.translation: لكن ماذا كان بإمكان أي منا أن يفعل؟ كانت ثورا غراي الشخص الوحيد الذي قد يكون قادراً على التعرف على القاتل.

sentences.text: She wasn't calm and quiet now. She was almost crying, and her hands were shaking.
sentences.translation: لم تكن هادئة وهادئة الآن. كانت على وشك البكاء، وكانت يداها ترتجفان.

sentences.text: 'I never really looked at him,' she said. 'What a fool I was! Even if I see him again, I might not recognise him. I've got a bad memory for faces.'
sentences.translation: قالت.

sentences.text: Poirot put his hand gently on her shoulder, 'Now, little one, don't be upset,' he said kindly.
sentences.translation: وضع بوارو يده بلطف على كتفها،
قال بلطف.

sentences.text: 'If you see this man, you will recognise him. We have had a lot of bad luck, and our murderer has had a lot of good luck.'
But now I believe that our luck has changed! The clue of the stockings is the beginning. Now every thing will go wrong for him! He, too, will begin to make mistakes...'
sentences.translation: لكنني أعتقد الآن أن حظنا قد تغير! دليل الجوارب هو البداية. الآن سيسوء كل شيء بالنسبة له! هو أيضاً سيبدأ في ارتكاب الأخطاء...

sentences.text: We had agreed that we would walk round as many streets as possible, and later, position ourselves in different parts of the race-course.
sentences.translation: كنا قد اتفقنا أننا سوف نسير في أكبر عدد ممكن من الشوارع، ولاحقاً، نتمركز في أجزاء مختلفة من مضمار السباق.

sentences.text: I had suggested that I should go with one of the ladies, and Poirot had agreed with my idea.
sentences.translation: كنت قد اقترحت أن أذهب مع إحدى السيدات، ووافق بوارو على فكرتي.

sentences.text: The girls went to put on their hats. Franklin Clarke started to talk to Poirot.
sentences.translation: ذهبت الفتيات لارتداء قبعاتهن. بدأ فرانكلين كلارك يتحدث إلى بوارو.

sentences.text: 'Listen, Monsieur Poirot. You went down to Churston, I know, and saw my brother's wife.'
Did she say - I mean, did she suggest -?'
sentences.translation: هل قالت - أعني، هل اقترحت -؟

sentences.text: He stopped, embarrassed. Poirot looked at him with an innocent face.
sentences.translation: توقف، محرجاً. نظر إليه بوارو بوجه بريء.

sentences.text: 'Did she suggest - what?'
Franklin Clarke's face was rather red.
sentences.translation: كان وجه فرانكلين كلارك محمراً نوعاً ما.

sentences.text: 'It's about Thora - Miss Grey,' he said. Poirot looked surprised.
sentences.translation: قال. بدا بوارو مندهشاً.

sentences.text: 'Lady Clarke got certain ideas in her head. You see, Thora - Miss Grey - is rather a good-looking girl - and Lady Clarke became jealous.'
After Car's death, she got very upset. Of course it's partly the illness and the drugs.
sentences.translation: بعد وفاة كار، أصبحت مستاءة جداً. بالطبع جزء من ذلك هو المرض والأدوية.

sentences.text: 'My brother always said that Miss Grey was the best secretary he ever had - and he was very fond of her, too.'
But there wasn't any romantic relationship between them. Look,' - he put his hand in his pocket - 'here's a letter I received from my brother when I was in Asia.'
sentences.translation: لكن لم تكن هناك أي علاقة رومانسية بينهما. انظر،
هذه رسالة تلقيتها من أخي عندما كنت في آسيا.

sentences.text: You may remember Thora Grey? She is a dear girl and a great help to me. She loves beautiful things and shares my enthusiasm for Chinese art. I was very lucky to find her. No daughter could be closer to me.'
sentences.translation: قد تتذكر ثورا غراي؟ إنها فتاة عزيزة وعون كبير لي. تحب الأشياء الجميلة وتشاركني حماسي للفن الصيني. كنت محظوظًا جدًا بإيجادها. لا يمكن لأي ابنة أن تكون أقرب إليّ منها.

sentences.text: 'You see,' said Franklin. 'My brother thought of her like a daughter. I wanted to show you this, because I didn't want you to get the wrong idea about Thora from anything that Lady Clarke said.'
sentences.translation: قال فرانكلين.

sentences.text: Poirot returned the letter. 'You can be sure,' he said, smiling, 'that I never allow myself to get the wrong idea from anything that anyone tells me. I form my own judgements.'
sentences.translation: أعاد بوارو الرسالة.
قال، مبتسماً،

sentences.text: The girls came back and we left the room. Then Poirot called me back.
sentences.translation: عادت الفتيات وغادرنا الغرفة. ثم ناداني بوارو.

sentences.text: 'Which lady do you intend to go with, Hastings?' he asked.
sentences.translation: سأل.

sentences.text: 'Well - I - er - I hadn't thought about it yet.'
'What about Miss Barnard?'
'She's rather an independent type,' I said.
sentences.translation: قلت.

sentences.text: 'Miss Grey?'
'Yes. She's better.'
'Hastings, you are not being honest with me,' said Poirot. 'All the time you wanted to spend the day with Miss Grey'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: 'Oh, Poirot!' I said.
sentences.translation: قلت.

sentences.text: 'I am sorry to upset your plans,' said Poirot, 'but I request you to go with Mary Drower - and I must ask that you do not leave her.'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو،

sentences.text: 'But, Poirot, why?'
'Because, my dear friend, her name begins with a D. We must be very careful.'
I realised that Poirot was right. If A B C hated Poirot, he might be watching his movements. He might kill Mary Drower to show Poirot that he was cleverer than my friend.
sentences.translation: أدركت أن بوارو كان على حق. إذا كان A B C يكره بوارو، فقد يكون يراقب تحركاته. قد يقتل ماري دراور ليري بوارو أنه أذكى من صديقي.

sentences.text: I promised to do as Poirot asked.
sentences.translation: وعدت بفعل ما طلبه بوارو.

sentences.text: CHAPTER TEN
sentences.translation: الفصل العاشر

sentences.text: Death at the Cinema
sentences.translation: موت في السينما

sentences.text: Mr Leadbetter was at the Regal Cinema in Doncaster. At the most exciting part of the film, the man next to him got up and pushed past him.
sentences.translation: كان السيد ليدبيتر في سينما ريجال في دونكاستر. في أكثر أجزاء الفيلم إثارة، نهض الرجل الذي بجانبه ودفع من جانبه.

sentences.text: Then he dropped his hat over the seat in front and bent over to get it back. Mr Leadbetter was very annoyed.
sentences.translation: ثم أسقط قبعته على المقعد أمامه وانحنى ليستعيدها. كان السيد ليدبيتر منزعجاً جداً.

sentences.text: He had looked forward to seeing this film for a whole week. Why couldn't people wait until the end of a film?
sentences.translation: كان قد تطلع لمشاهدة هذا الفيلم لمدة أسبوع كامل. لماذا لا يستطيع الناس الانتظار حتى نهاية الفيلم؟

sentences.text: The annoying gentleman went out. Mr Leadbetter watched the film happily until the end.
sentences.translation: خرج السيد المزعج. شاهد السيد ليدبيتر الفيلم بسعادة حتى النهاية.

sentences.text: When the lights went up, he got up slowly. He never left the cinema very quickly.
sentences.translation: عندما أُضيئت الأنوار، نهض ببطء. لم يكن أبداً يغادر السينما بسرعة كبيرة.

sentences.text: He looked around. There weren't many people this afternoon - naturally.
sentences.translation: نظر حوله. لم يكن هناك الكثير من الناس بعد ظهر هذا اليوم - بطبيعة الحال.

sentences.text: It was the day of the St Leger and they were all at the races. Everyone was hurrying towards the exit.
sentences.translation: كان يوم سباق سانت ليجيه وكان الجميع في السباق. كان الجميع يسرع نحو المخرج.

sentences.text: Mr Leadbetter started to follow. The man in the seat in front of him was asleep.
sentences.translation: بدأ السيد ليدبيتر يتبع. كان الرجل في المقعد أمامه نائماً.

sentences.text: 'Excuse me, sir,' said a man who was trying to get past the sleeping gentleman.
sentences.translation: قال رجل كان يحاول المرور من جانب السيد النائم.

sentences.text: Mr Leadbetter reached the exit. He looked back. Something seemed to be happening... perhaps the man in front of him was drunk and not asleep...
sentences.translation: وصل السيد ليدبيتر إلى المخرج. نظر إلى الوراء. بدا أن شيئاً ما يحدث... ربما كان الرجل أمامه ثملاً وليس نائماً...

sentences.text: He stopped for a moment, and then went out.
sentences.translation: توقف للحظة، ثم خرج.

sentences.text: The manager was saying to the man who had tried to get past, 'He's ill...' He spoke to the sleeping man. 'What's the matter, sir?'
sentences.translation: كان المدير يقول للرجل الذي حاول المرور:
تحدث إلى الرجل النائم.

sentences.text: The other man touched the sleeper. He took his hand away, and looked at a red sticky mark.
sentences.translation: لمس الرجل الآخر النائم. سحب يده ونظر إلى علامة حمراء لزجة.

sentences.text: 'Blood...'
The manager saw the corner of something under the seat.
sentences.translation: رأى المدير طرف شيء ما تحت المقعد.

sentences.text: 'It's at - ABC,' he said.
sentences.translation: قال.

sentences.text: Mr Cust left the Regal Cinema and looked up at the sky. It was a beautiful evening... a, really beautiful evening...
sentences.translation: غادر السيد كاست سينما ريجال ونظر إلى السماء. كان مساءً جميلاً... مساءً جميلاً حقاً...

sentences.text: He walked along smiling to himself until he came to the Black Horse, where he was staying.
sentences.translation: سار مبتسماً لنفسه حتى وصل إلى بلاك هورس، حيث كان يقيم.

sentences.text: He climbed the stairs to his bedroom, a small room on the second floor. As he entered the room, he suddenly stopped smiling.
sentences.translation: صعد الدرج إلى غرفة نومه، غرفة صغيرة في الطابق الثاني. عندما دخل الغرفة، توقف فجأة عن الابتسام.

sentences.text: There was a mark on the arm of his coat. He touched it - wet and red - blood...
sentences.translation: كانت هناك علامة على ذراع معطفه. لمسها - رطبة وحمراء - دم...

sentences.text: He put his hand in his pocket and brought out something - a long thin knife... that was sticky and red...
sentences.translation: وضع يده في جيبه وأخرج شيئاً - سكيناً طويلاً رفيعاً... كان لزجاً وأحمر...

sentences.text: Mr Cust sat down and looted around the room like a hunted animal.
sentences.translation: جلس السيد كاست ونظر حول الغرفة مثل حيوان مطارد.

sentences.text: 'It isn't my fault,' he said, he passed his tongue over his lips.
sentences.translation: قال، ومرر لسانه على شفتيه.

sentences.text: Then he went over to the sink and filled it with water. He took off his coat and washed the arm. The water was red now...
sentences.translation: ثم ذهب إلى الحوض وملأه بالماء. خلع معطفه وغسل ذراعه. أصبح الماء أحمر الآن...

sentences.text: There was a knock on the door. He stood there, frown with fear. The door opened. It was a young woman carrying some water.
sentences.translation: كان هناك طرق على الباب. وقف هناك، عابساً من الخوف. فُتح الباب. كانت شابة تحمل بعض الماء.

sentences.text: 'Oh, excuse me, sir. Your hot water, sir.'
'Thank you... I've washed in cold water...' Immediately she looked at the water in the sink. 'I've cut my hand...' said Mr Cust quickly.
sentences.translation: فوراً نظرت إلى الماء في الحوض.
قال السيد كاست بسرعة.

sentences.text: There was a pause - yes surely a very long pause - before she said, 'Yes, sir.'
sentences.translation: كان هناك توقف - نعم بالتأكيد توقف طويل جداً - قبل أن تقول:

sentences.text: She went out, shutting the door; Mr Cust stood and listened.
sentences.translation: خرجت، مغلقة الباب؛ وقف السيد كاست واستمع.

sentences.text: Were there voices - feet coming up the stirs? He could hear only the beating of his own heart. Then suddenly he moved.
sentences.translation: هل كانت هناك أصوات - أقدام تصعد الدرج؟ كان يسمع فقط دقات قلبه. ثم تحرك فجأة.

sentences.text: He put on his coat, went to the door and opened it. There no one outside. He went quietly down the stairs.
sentences.translation: ارتدى معطفه، وذهب إلى الباب وفتحه. لم يكن هناك أحد في الخارج. نزل الدرج بهدوء.

sentences.text: He ran out of the door that opened onto the hotel car park. A couple of drivers wars there, talking about the races.
sentences.translation: ركض خارجاً من الباب الذي يفتح على موقف سيارات الفندق. كان هناك سائقان يتحدثان عن السباق.

sentences.text: Mr Cust hurried across the car park and out into the street. Should he go to the station? Yes - there would be crowds there - special trains.
sentences.translation: أسرع السيد كاست عبر موقف السيارات وخرج إلى الشارع. هل يجب أن يذهب إلى المحطة؟ نعم - سيكون هناك حشود - قطارات خاصة.

sentences.text: With a bit of luck, he could get away.
sentences.translation: مع قليل من الحظ، يمكنه الهرب.

sentences.text: Inspector Crome was interviewing Mr Leadbetter. The Chief Constable, Colonel Anderson, was there, too.
sentences.translation: كان المفتش كروم يستجوب السيد ليدبيتر. كان رئيس الشرطة، الكولونيل أندرسون، هناك أيضاً.

sentences.text: 'Please tell me everything clearly,' said Crome. 'This man went out towards the end of the main film? As he passed you, he fell -'
sentences.translation: قال كروم.

sentences.text: 'He pretended to fall. I understand it now. He bent over the seat in front to pick up his hat. He surely stabbed the man then. Then he went out.'
'Can you describe him?'
'He was a very big man.'
'Fair or dark?'
'I - well, I'm not exactly sure. He was an ugly-looking man.'
Inspector Crome nodded. Then he interviewed the cinema manager. The manager told Crome about the blood on the dead man's coat and the ABC railway guide under the seat.
sentences.translation: أومأ المفتش كروم. ثم استجوب مدير السينما. أخبر المدير كروم عن الدم على معطف الرجل الميت ودليل سكك حديدية ABC تحت المقعد.

sentences.text: 'Did you notice a man leaving the cinema a few minutes earlier?'
'There were several, sir.'
Just then a police constable came in. 'Mr Hercule Poirot's here, sir, and another gentleman.'
sentences.translation: في تلك اللحظة دخل شرطي.

sentences.text: Inspector Crome didn't look pleased. 'Oh, well,' he said. 'They'd better come in, I suppose.'
sentences.translation: لم يبدُ المفتش كروم سعيداً.
قال.

sentences.text: Poirot and I entered the room. Both Crome and Colonel Anderson were looking worried. Colonel Anderson greeted us with a nod of the head.
sentences.translation: دخل بوارو وأنا الغرفة. كان كل من كروم والكولونيل أندرسون يبدوان قلقين. استقبلنا الكولونيل أندرسون بإيماءة من الرأس.

sentences.text: 'I'm glad you've come, Monsieur Poirot,' he said politely.
sentences.translation: قال بأدب.

sentences.text: 'Another ABC murder?'
'Yes. The murderer bent over and stabbed the victim in the back. There was an ABC on the floor between the dead man's feet.'
'Do you know who the dead man is?' asked Poirot.
sentences.translation: سأل بوارو.

sentences.text: 'Yes, I think A B C's made a mistake this time. The dead man is called Earlsfield - George Earlsfield. He missed out the letter D.'
My friend shook his head doubtfully.
sentences.translation: هز صديقي رأسه بشك.

sentences.text: 'Shall we talk to the man who found him?' asked Crome. 'He's anxious to get home.'
sentences.translation: سأل كروم.

sentences.text: A middle-aged gentleman came in. He spoke in an excited, high voice.
sentences.translation: دخل رجل في منتصف العمر. تحدث بصوت مرتفع متحمس.

sentences.text: 'It's the most shocking experience I've ever known,' he said.
sentences.translation: قال.

sentences.text: 'Your name, please,' said the Inspector.
sentences.translation: قال المفتش.

sentences.text: 'Downes. Roger Emmanuel Downes. I'm a teacher at a boys' school.'
'Now, Mr Downes, please tell us in your own words what happened.'
At the end of the film I got up from my seat. The seat on my left was empty but in the seat next to that there was a man who seemed to be asleep.
sentences.translation: في نهاية الفيلم نهضت من مقعدي. كان المقعد على يساري فارغاً لكن في المقعد المجاور لذلك كان هناك رجل يبدو نائماً.

sentences.text: I realised that he was ill, and I called out,
As I couldn't pass him, I put my hand on his shoulder to wake him.
sentences.translation: أدركت أنه مريض، وناديت:
بما أنني لم أستطع المرور من جانبه، وضعت يدي على كتفه لأوقظه.

sentences.text: Then I took my hand from the man's shoulder. I found that it was wet and red...'
sentences.translation: ثم سحبت يدي من كتف الرجل. وجدت أنها كانت رطبة وحمراء...

sentences.text: Colonel Anderson was looking at Mr Downes.
sentences.translation: كان الكولونيل أندرسون ينظر إلى السيد داونز.

sentences.text: 'Mr Downes, you're a very lucky man. You're about the same height as the dead man. I think the murderer became confused.'
He followed you into the cinema but he chose the wrong victim. I am sure, Mr Downes, that that knife was meant for you!'
sentences.translation: لقد تبعك إلى السينما لكنه اختار الضحية الخاطئة. أنا متأكد يا سيد داونز، أن تلك السكين كانت لك!

sentences.text: Mr Downes became weak with shock. He sat down on a chair.
sentences.translation: أصبح السيد داونز ضعيفاً من الصدمة. جلس على كرسي.

sentences.text: 'You mean that this madman has followed me? But why me?'
He got up. He suddenly looked old and shaken. 'If you don't want me anymore, gentlemen, I think I'll go home. I - I don't feel very well.'
sentences.translation: نهض. بدا فجأة عجوزاً ومرتجفاً.

sentences.text: Mr Downes left the room.
sentences.translation: غادر السيد داونز الغرفة.

sentences.text: 'Send couple of constables to watch his house,' said Colonel Anderson.
sentences.translation: قال الكولونيل أندرسون.

sentences.text: 'You think,' said Poirot, 'that when ABC finds out his mistake, he might try to murder Mr Downes again?'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو،

sentences.text: Anderson nodded. 'It's a possibility,' he said. A B C may be upset if things don't go according to his plans.'
sentences.translation: أومأ أندرسون.
قال.

sentences.text: A constable came in. 'Mr Ball of the Black Horse is here with a young woman, sir,' he said.
sentences.translation: دخل شرطي.
قال.

sentences.text: 'He thinks he has something to tell you which may be helpful.'
Mr Ball was a large, slow-thinking, heavily-moving man. He smelled strongly of beer. With him there was a young woman with round eyes. She seemed to be very excited.
sentences.translation: كان السيد بول رجلاً ضخماً، بطيء التفكير، ثقيل الحركة. كانت تفوح منه رائحة البيرة بقوة. كان معه شابة بعينين مستديرتين. بدت متحمسة جداً.

sentences.text: 'This girl, Mary, has something to tell you,' said Mr Ball.
sentences.translation: قال السيد بول.

sentences.text: Mary told us that she had taken hot water to one of the hotel guests in his room. He was washing his hands.
sentences.translation: أخبرتنا ماري أنها كانت قد أخذت ماءً ساخناً لأحد نزلاء الفندق في غرفته. كان يغسل يديه.

sentences.text: He had taken his coat off and was holding the arm of it in the water in the sink. The coat was wet and the water in the sink was red.
sentences.translation: كان قد خلع معطفه وكان يمسك ذراعه في الماء في الحوض. كان المعطف مبللاً والماء في الحوض أحمر.

sentences.text: 'Red?' said Anderson sharply. 'When was this?'
sentences.translation: قال أندرسون بحدة.

sentences.text: 'At about a quarter to five.'
'More than three hours ago,' said Anderson. 'Why didn't you come at once?'
sentences.translation: قال أندرسون.

sentences.text: 'We didn't know that there'd been another murder,' said Ball. 'When we heard the news, Mary screamed out about the blood in the sink.'
sentences.translation: قال بول.

sentences.text: I went upstairs to the room, but there was nobody there. One of the men in the car park said he saw a man leaving. So I told Mary to come to the police.'
sentences.translation: صعدت إلى الغرفة، لكن لم يكن هناك أحد. قال أحد الرجال في موقف السيارات إنه رأى رجلاً يغادر. لذا أخبرت ماري أن تأتي إلى الشرطة.

sentences.text: 'Describe this man,' said Inspector Crome to Mary.
sentences.translation: قال المفتش كروم لماري.

sentences.text: 'He wasn't very tall or short,' said Mary. 'And he stooped and wore glasses. He was wearing a dark suit and a hat. His clothes looked old and cheap.'
sentences.translation: قالت ماري.

sentences.text: Inspector Crome sent two men to the Black Horse. They came back about ten minutes later and brought the hotel book, which all guests had to sign.
sentences.translation: أرسل المفتش كروم رجلين إلى بلاك هورس. عادا بعد حوالي عشر دقائق وأحضرا سجل الفندق، الذي كان على جميع النزلاء التوقيع فيه.

sentences.text: We crowded around it. There was a signature there in small writing.
sentences.translation: تجمّعنا حوله. كانت هناك توقيع بخط صغير.

sentences.text: 'A B Case - or is it Cash?' said Colonel Anderson.
sentences.translation: قال الكولونيل أندرسون.

sentences.text: 'A B C,' said Crome.
sentences.translation: قال كروم.

sentences.text: 'What about his luggage?' asked Anderson.
sentences.translation: سأل أندرسون.

sentences.text: 'We found a suitcase in his room, sir, full of small boxes.'
'What was in them?'
'Stockings, sir.'
'Congratulations,' Crome said to Poirot. 'Your guess was right.'
sentences.translation: قال كروم لبوارو.

sentences.text: Inspector Crome was in his office at Scotland Yard. The telephone on his desk rang. It was one of the policemen who was helping him on the case.
sentences.translation: كان المفتش كروم في مكتبه في سكوتلاند يارد. رن الهاتف على مكتبه. كان أحد رجال الشرطة الذين يساعدونه في القضية.

sentences.text: 'Jacobs speaking, sir. A man has come with a story that you ought to hear.'
A few minutes later there was a knock on the door. Jacobs appeared with a tall young man.
sentences.translation: بعد بضع دقائق كان هناك طرق على الباب. ظهر جيكوبز مع شاب طويل.

sentences.text: 'This is Mr Tom Hartigan, sir. He's got something to tell us- which may be important in the ABC case.'
The Inspector got up and shook hands with the visitor.
sentences.translation: نهض المفتش وصافح الزائر.

sentences.text: 'Good morning, Mr Hartigan. Sit down. What do you want to tell me?'
'Well,' began Tom nervously, 'I've got a young lady friend, you see, and her mother rents out rooms in her house. One of the rooms has been rented for over two years to a man called Cust.'
sentences.translation: بدأ توم بتوتر،

sentences.text: Tom told the Inspector about his meeting with Mr Cust at Euston Station, and the ticket for Doncaster which Mr Cust had dropped.
sentences.translation: أخبر توم المفتش عن لقائه بالسيد كاست في محطة يوستون، والتذكرة إلى دونكاستر التي أسقطها السيد كاست.

sentences.text: 'Lily - my young lady - also told me that Mr Cust was near Churston at the time of the murder, and at the seaside when the Bexhill murder happened.'
'The newspapers said that information was wanted about A B Case or Cash. Lily's mother, Mrs Marbury, told me that Mr Cust is A B Cust.'
Then we wondered if Mr Cust had been away from home on the date of the Andover murder. And we remembered that he was.'
sentences.translation: ثم تساءلنا إن كان السيد كاست قد كان بعيداً عن المنزل في تاريخ جريمة أندوفر. وتذكرنا أنه كان كذلك.

sentences.text: Inspector Crome listened to everything carefully. 'You were quite right to come here,' he said.
sentences.translation: استمع المفتش كروم إلى كل شيء بعناية.
قال.

sentences.text: 'These dates may be only a coincidence, and the name, too. But I'd certainly like to interview Mr Cust. Is he at home now?'
'Yes, sir.'
'When did he return?'
'On the evening of the Doncaster murder, sir. He's stayed in a lot since then. And he doesn't look very well, Mrs Marbury says.'
He buys a lot of newspapers. Mrs Marbury says that he talks to himself, too.'
sentences.translation: يشتري الكثير من الصحف. تقول السيدة ماربوري إنه يتحدث مع نفسه أيضاً.

sentences.text: Tom gave Inspector Crome Mrs Marbury's address.
sentences.translation: أعطى توم المفتش كروم عنوان السيدة ماربوري.

sentences.text: 'Thank you,' said the Inspector. 'I shall probably visit the house later today. Please be careful if you meet Mr Cust. Good morning, Mr Hartigan.'
sentences.translation: قال المفتش.

sentences.text: Tom went outside. Lily Marbury was waiting for him. He told her about his meeting with Inspector Crome.
sentences.translation: خرج توم. كانت ليلي ماربوري تنتظره. أخبرها عن لقائه بالمفتش كروم.

sentences.text: 'The police are going to come and ask him some questions,' he said.
sentences.translation: قال.

sentences.text: 'Poor Mr Cust,' said Lily.
sentences.translation: قالت ليلي.

sentences.text: 'Don't feel scary for him. If he's ABC, he's murdered four people.'
Lily shook her head. 'It does seem awful,' she said.
sentences.translation: هزت ليلي رأسها.
قالت.

sentences.text: 'Come and have some lunch,' said Tom.
sentences.translation: قال توم.

sentences.text: 'All right. But I must just telephone someone. A girl I going to meet.'
She ran across the road and came back, looking rather red in the face. She put her arm through Tom's arm.
sentences.translation: ركضت عبر الطريق وعادت، وبدا وجهها محمراً نوعاً ما. وضعت ذراعها في ذراع توم.

sentences.text: 'Tell me more about Scotland Yard. You didn't see the other man there! The Belgian gentleman. The one that ABC writes to.'
'No. He wasn't there.'
'Well, tell me all about it. Who did you speak to and what did you say?'
Mr Cust put the phone back very gently. He turned to where Mrs Marbury was standing watching him.
sentences.translation: أعاد السيد كاست الهاتف بلطف شديد. التفت إلى حيث كانت السيدة ماربوري واقفة تراقبه.

sentences.text: 'You don't often have a telephone call, Mr Cust,' she said. 'I hope it's not bad news?'
sentences.translation: قالت.

sentences.text: 'No - no.' He saw that Mrs Marbury was holding a newspaper. He read Births - Marriages - Deaths...
sentences.translation: رأى أن السيدة ماربوري تحمل صحيفة. قرأ المواليد - الزيجات - الوفيات...

sentences.text: 'My sister's just had a little boy,' he said quickly.
sentences.translation: قال بسرعة.

sentences.text: 'Well, that is nice,' said Mrs Marbury. She wondered why Mr Cust had never said he had a sister.
sentences.translation: قالت السيدة ماربوري. تساءلت لماذا لم يذكر السيد كاست أبداً أن لديه أختاً.

sentences.text: 'Well. Mr Cust, my congratulations. Is it the first one, or have you other little nephews and nieces?'
'It's the only one,' said Mr Cust. The only one I've ever had or am likely to have and - er - I think I must go there at once.'
sentences.translation: قال السيد كاست.

sentences.text: They - they want me to come. I - I think I can just catch a train if I hurry.'
sentences.translation: إنهم - إنهم يريدونني أن آتي. أنا - أعتقد أنني يمكن أن ألحق بقطار إذا أسرعت.

sentences.text: 'Will you be away long, Mr Cust?' called Mrs Marbury he ran up the stairs.
sentences.translation: نادت السيدة ماربوري بينما كان يركض صعوداً على الدرج.

sentences.text: 'Oh, no two or three days, that's all.'
He disappeared into his bedroom. A few minutes later, he came quietly down the stairs carrying a bag in his hand.
sentences.translation: اختفى في غرفة نومه. بعد بضع دقائق، نزل الدرج بهدوء حاملاً حقيبة في يده.

sentences.text: He saw the telephone and remembered the short conversation he had just had.
sentences.translation: رأى الهاتف وتذكر المحادثة القصيرة التي أجراها للتو.

sentences.text: 'Is that you, Mr Cust? I thought you might like to know that an inspector from Scotland Yard may come to see you...'
Why had Lily telephoned him? Had she guessed his secret? How did she know that the Inspector was coming? Did she know...
sentences.translation: لماذا اتصلت به ليلي؟ هل خمّنت سره؟ كيف عرفت أن المفتش قادم؟ هل تعرف...

sentences.text: But it surely if she knew, she wouldn't... Women were very strange, surprisingly cruel and surprisingly kind. Lily was a kind girl. A kind, pretty girl.
sentences.translation: لكن بالتأكيد لو كانت تعرف، لما... النساء غريبات جداً، قاسيات بشكل مفاجئ ولطيفات بشكل مفاجئ. كانت ليلي فتاة طيبة. فتاة طيبة وجميلة.

sentences.text: He paused in the hall. Then he heard a noise from the kitchen.
sentences.translation: توقف في القاعة. ثم سمع ضجيجاً من المطبخ.

sentences.text: Mrs Marbury might come out..
sentences.translation: قد تخرج السيدة ماربوري..

sentences.text: He opened the front door, passed through it and closed it behind him.
sentences.translation: فتح الباب الأمامي، ومر عبره وأغلقه خلفه.

sentences.text: Where...?
sentences.translation: إلى أين...؟

sentences.text: Poirot and I were having another meeting with the Chief Constable, Colonel Anderson and Inspector Crome.
sentences.translation: كان بوارو وأنا في اجتماع آخر مع رئيس الشرطة، الكولونيل أندرسون والمفتش كروم.

sentences.text: 'I've got a list of people in the Churston area where the man went and offered stockings,' said Inspector Crome.'
sentences.translation: قال المفتش كروم.

sentences.text: 'He stayed at a small hotel. He returned there at 10.30 on the night of the murder.'
'He did the same thing in Bexhill. He stayed at a hotel under his own name, and offered stockings to people at about twelve addresses, including Mrs Barnard and including the Orange Cat.'
He did the same in Andover. He stayed at a small hotel there, too, and offered stockings to Mrs Fowler, next door to Mrs Ascher, and to several other people in the same street.
sentences.translation: فعل نفس الشيء في أندوفر. أقام في فندق صغير هناك أيضاً، وعرض الجوارب على السيدة فاولر، الجارة المجاورة للسيدة آشر، وعلى عدة أشخاص آخرين في نفس الشارع.

sentences.text: 'I went to the address which Mr Hartigan gave me,' said the Inspector, 'but I found that Cust had left the house about half an hour before.'
sentences.translation: قال المفتش،

sentences.text: He received a telephone message. Mrs Marbury said it was the first time.
sentences.translation: تلقى رسالة هاتفية. قالت السيدة ماربوري إنها كانت المرة الأولى.

sentences.text: 'I searched his room very carefully. I found notepaper there similar to the paper which the letters were written on.'
There was also a strange quantity of stockings - and at the back of the same cupboard there were eight new ABC railway guides!'
sentences.translation: كانت هناك أيضاً كمية غريبة من الجوارب - وفي الجزء الخلفي من نفس الخزانة كانت هناك ثمانية أدلة سكك حديدية ABC جديدة!

sentences.text: 'That proves he's guilty,' said Colonel Anderson.
sentences.translation: قال الكولونيل أندرسون.

sentences.text: 'I've found something else, too, said the Inspector. 'I only found it this morning, sir.'
sentences.translation: قال المفتش.

sentences.text: There was no sign of the knife in his room, but I thought perhaps he'd brought it back to the house and hidden it somewhere. I found it immediately.
sentences.translation: لم يكن هناك أثر للسكين في غرفته، لكنني اعتقدت أنه ربما أحضرها إلى المنزل وأخفاها في مكان ما. وجدتها فوراً.

sentences.text: The coatstand - no one ever moves a coatstand. I moved it away from the wall - and there it was! The knife! The dried blood was still on it.'
sentences.translation: حاملة المعاطف - لا أحد يحرك حاملة المعاطف أبداً. أزحتها بعيداً عن الحائط - وكانت هناك! السكين! كان الدم الجاف لا يزال عليها.

sentences.text: 'Good work, Crome,' said Colonel Anderson. 'We only need one thing more now. The man himself.'
sentences.translation: قال الكولونيل أندرسون.

sentences.text: 'Don't worry, we'll get him,' said Crome.
sentences.translation: قال كروم.

sentences.text: 'But there is something that worries me very much,' said Poirot. 'It is the why? The motive.'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: 'But, my dear Poirot, the man's crazy,' said Colonel Anderson impatiently. 'Well, as you say, Crome, it's just a matter of time before we find him.'
sentences.translation: قال الكولونيل أندرسون بنفاد صبر.

sentences.text: Mr Cust stood by a fruit and vegetable shop, staring across the road. Yes, that was it, A. Ascher, Newsagent. In the empty window there was a sign: 'Shop to Rent.'
sentences.translation: وقف السيد كاست بجانب متجر فواكه وخضروات، محدقاً عبر الطريق. نعم، كان ذلك هو، أ. آشر، بائع صحف. في النافذة الفارغة كانت هناك لافتة:

sentences.text: He walked slowly back towards the mam street of the town. It was difficult - very difficult - now that he hadn't any more money... He hadn't had anything to eat all day.
sentences.translation: سار ببطء عائداً نحو الشارع الرئيسي في البلدة. كان الأمر صعباً - صعباً جداً - الآن بعد أن لم يكن لديه أي مال... لم يكن قد أكل أي شيء طوال اليوم.

sentences.text: He looked at a board outside another newsagent's shop.
sentences.translation: نظر إلى لوحة خارج متجر بائع صحف آخر.

sentences.text: HE ABC CASE. MURDERER STILL FREE.
sentences.translation: قضية ABC. القاتل لا يزال طليقاً.

sentences.text: Interviews with Hercule Poirot. Mr Cust said to himself, 'Hercule Poirot. I wonder if he knows.' He continued walking.
sentences.translation: مقابلات مع هرقل بوارو. قال السيد كاست لنفسه:
تابع السير.

sentences.text: Where was he going? He didn't know. He had come to the end.
sentences.translation: إلى أين كان ذاهباً؟ لم يكن يعرف. لقد وصل إلى النهاية.

sentences.text: He looked up. There were lights in front of him. And letters... Police Station.
sentences.translation: رفع رأسه. كانت هناك أضواء أمامه. وحروف... مركز الشرطة.

sentences.text: 'That's funny? said Mr Cust. He gave a little laugh.
sentences.translation: قال السيد كاست. أطلق ضحكة صغيرة.

sentences.text: Then he stepped inside. Suddenly, as he did so, he fell forward.
sentences.translation: ثم دخل إلى الداخل. فجأة، وبينما كان يفعل ذلك، سقط إلى الأمام.

sentences.text: CHAPTER ELEVEN
sentences.translation: الفصل الحادي عشر

sentences.text: And Catch a Fox
sentences.translation: والإمساك بالثعلب

sentences.text: It was a clear November day. Dr Thompson and Chief Inspector Japp had come to tell Poirot about the police case against Alexander Bonaparte Cust.
sentences.translation: كان يوماً صافياً من نوفمبر. جاء الدكتور طومسون والمفتش الرئيسي جاب لإخبار بوارو عن قضية الشرطة ضد ألكسندر بونابرت كاست.

sentences.text: 'What's your opinion of Cust?' Poirot asked Dr Thompson.
sentences.translation: سأل بوارو الدكتور طومسون.

sentences.text: 'I don't know. He doesn't seem to be mad. He's an epileptic, of course.'
'Yes, that was clear when he fell into the police station in Andover,' I said.
sentences.translation: قلت.

sentences.text: 'But can a man murder someone and not know they've done it?'
'In my opinion Cust knows very well that he's responsible for murder,' said Dr Thompson.
sentences.translation: قال الدكتور طومسون.

sentences.text: 'The letters prove that the murders were planned crimes.'
'And we still have no explanation for the letters,' said Poirot.
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: 'Until I know why they were written, I shall not feel that the case is solved.'
'Well, I must go,' said Dr Thompson.
sentences.translation: قال الدكتور طومسون.

sentences.text: He went out. Japp stayed.
sentences.translation: خرج. بقي جاب.

sentences.text: 'So Cust has an alibi for the Bexhill murder,' said Poirot.
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: 'Yes,' said the Inspector. And his alibi is very strong. A man called Strange has told us that he met Cust in the Whitecross Hotel in Eastbourne on the evening of 24 July.
sentences.translation: قال المفتش.

sentences.text: After dinner he and Cust played cards. Cust played very well. They played cards until midnight, and separated at ten minutes past midnight.
sentences.translation: بعد العشاء لعب هو وكاست الورق. لعب كاست جيداً جداً. لعبوا الورق حتى منتصف الليل، وانفصلا في الساعة الثانية عشرة وعشر دقائق.

sentences.text: So if Cust was in a hotel in Eastbourne at that time, he couldn't strangle Betty Barnard on the beach at Bexhill between midnight and one o'clock.
sentences.translation: إذن إذا كان كاست في فندق في إيستبورن في ذلك الوقت، لم يكن بإمكانه خنق بيتي بارنارد على الشاطئ في بيكسهيل بين منتصف الليل والواحدة.

sentences.text: Eastbourne is about twenty-two kilometres away from Bexhill and it would take some time for him to get there.'
sentences.translation: إيستبورن على بعد حوالي اثنين وعشرين كيلومتراً من بيكسهيل وسيستغرق وصوله إلى هناك بعض الوقت.

sentences.text: 'It is a problem - yes,' said Poirot.
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: 'We know that Cust carried out the Doncaster murder - the coat with the blood, the knife - that's certain.'
He carried out the Churston murder. He carried out the Andover murder. So he also did the Bexhill murder. But I don't understand how!'
sentences.translation: نفذ جريمة تشيرستون. نفذ جريمة أندوفر. إذن فقد فعل جريمة بيكسهيل أيضاً. لكنني لا أفهم كيف!

sentences.text: 'Tell me, Hastings,' said Poirot, after Japp had gone. 'Do you think the case is finished?'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو، بعد أن ذهب جاب.

sentences.text: 'Well - yes. We've got the man. And we've got most of the facts.'
Poirot shook his head.
sentences.translation: هز بوارو رأسه.

sentences.text: 'But until we know all about the man, the mystery is as deep as ever. And we know nothing at all!'
We know where he was born. We know that he fought in the war and was hit on the head. We know that he left the army because he is an epileptic.
sentences.translation: نعرف أين وُلد. نعرف أنه قاتل في الحرب وأُصيب في رأسه. نعرف أنه ترك الجيش لأنه مصاب بالصرع.

sentences.text: We know that he rented a room from Mrs Marbury. We know that he is very quiet and shy - the kind of man that nobody notices.
sentences.translation: نعرف أنه استأجر غرفة من السيدة ماربوري. نعرف أنه هادئ وخجول جداً - نوع الرجل الذي لا يلاحظه أحد.

sentences.text: 'We know that he planned and carried out several very clever murders. We know that he made some stupid mistakes.'
We know that he killed without pity. We know that he did not want anyone else to suffer for his crimes.
sentences.translation: نعرف أنه قتل بلا رحمة. نعرف أنه لم يرد أن يعاني أي شخص آخر بسبب جرائمه.

sentences.text: Do you not see, Hastings, that the man is like two different people?
sentences.translation: ألا ترى يا هاستينغز، أن الرجل يشبه شخصين مختلفين؟

sentences.text: 'All the time I have tried to get to know the murderer. And now I realise, Hastings, that I do not know him at all!'
I am quite confused. Why did he carry out these murders? Why did he choose those people?'
sentences.translation: أنا مرتبك تماماً. لماذا نفذ جرائم القتل هذه؟ لماذا اختار هؤلاء الأشخاص؟

sentences.text: 'Alphabetically -' I began.
sentences.translation: بدأت.

sentences.text: 'Was Betty Barnard the only person in Bexhill whose name began with a B?'
Betty Barnard - I had an idea there... It ought to be true - it must be true. But if it is -'
sentences.translation: بيتي بارنارد - كانت لدي فكرة هناك... يجب أن تكون صحيحة - لا بد أن تكون صحيحة. لكن إذا كانت كذلك -

sentences.text: He was silent for some time. I didn't like to interrupt him, and I believe I fell asleep.
sentences.translation: صمت لبعض الوقت. لم أرد مقاطعته، وأعتقد أنني نمت.

sentences.text: Suddenly I woke to find Poirot's hand on my shoulder.
sentences.translation: فجأة استيقظت لأجد يد بوارو على كتفي.

sentences.text: 'Mon cher Hastings,' he said. 'Always you help me - you bring me luck.'
sentences.translation: قال.

sentences.text: I was quite confused. 'How have I helped you this time?' I asked.
sentences.translation: كنت مرتبكاً تماماً.
سألت.

sentences.text: 'I remembered something that you said. It makes everything very clear.'

I see the answers to all my questions. The reason for Mrs Ascher, the reason for Sir Carmichael Clarke, the reason for the Doncaster murder, and finally - very important - the reason for Hercule Poirot.
sentences.translation: أرى إجابات جميع أسئلتي. سبب السيدة آشر، سبب السير كارمايكل كلارك، سبب جريمة دونكاستر، وأخيراً - وهذا مهم جداً - السبب وراء هرقل بوارو.

sentences.text: 'But first, I need a little more information from our Special Legion.'
And then - then, when I have got an answer to one of my questions, I will go and see A B C. We will face each other at last - ABC and Hercule Poirot - the enemies. And then - we will talk!'
sentences.translation: وبعد ذلك - ثم، عندما أحصل على إجابة لأحد أسئلتي، سأذهب لرؤية A B C. سنواجه بعضنا البعض أخيراً - ABC وهرقل بوارو - الأعداء. وبعد ذلك - سنتحدث!

sentences.text: 'What do you expect Cust to tell you?' I asked.
sentences.translation: سألت.

sentences.text: Hercule Poirot smiled. 'A lie,' he said. 'And from the lie, I shall know the truth!'
sentences.translation: ابتسم هرقل بوارو.
قال.

sentences.text: During the next few days, Poirot was very busy. He was mysteriously absent for a lot of the time.
sentences.translation: خلال الأيام القليلة التالية، كان بوارو مشغولاً جداً. كان غائباً بشكل غامض معظم الوقت.

sentences.text: He talked very little and refused to answer any of my questions. But towards the end of the week, he said he intended to visit Bexhill.
sentences.translation: تحدث قليلاً جداً ورفض الإجابة على أي من أسئلتي. لكن نحو نهاية الأسبوع، قال إنه ينوي زيارة بيكسهيل.

sentences.text: He suggested that I should come with him and I agreed enthusiastically. The members of our Special Legion were also invited.
sentences.translation: اقترح أن آتي معه ووافقت بحماس. كما دُعي أعضاء فيلقنا الخاص أيضاً.

sentences.text: Poirot first visited Mr and Mrs Barnard and asked them when exactly Cust had come to their door, and what he had said.
sentences.translation: زار بوارو أولاً السيد والسيدة بارنارد وسألهما متى بالضبط جاء كاست إلى بابهما، وماذا قال.

sentences.text: Then he went to the hotel where Cust had stayed and asked for a detailed description of Cust.
sentences.translation: ثم ذهب إلى الفندق الذي أقام فيه كاست وطلب وصفاً تفصيلياً لكاست.

sentences.text: Next, he went to the beach - to the place where Betty Barnard's body had been discovered. He studied the ground carefully.
sentences.translation: بعد ذلك، ذهب إلى الشاطئ - إلى المكان الذي وُجدت فيه جثة بيتي بارنارد. درس الأرض بعناية.

sentences.text: He then walked from the beach to the nearest place where a car could be parked. From there he went to the place where the Eastbourne buses waited before leaving Bexhill.
sentences.translation: ثم سار من الشاطئ إلى أقرب مكان يمكن ركن سيارة فيه. من هناك ذهب إلى المكان الذي كانت تنتظر فيه حافلات إيستبورن قبل مغادرة بيكسهيل.

sentences.text: Finally he took us all to the Orange Cat cafe, where the fat waitress, Milly Higley, served us tea.
sentences.translation: أخيراً أخذنا جميعاً إلى مقهى أورنج كات، حيث قدمت لنا النادلة السمينة، ميلي هيغلي، الشاي.

sentences.text: 'I have finished in Bexhill,' said Poirot. 'I will go to Eastbourne. I need to ask one question there. It is not necessary for you all to come with me.'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: But come back to the hotel and let us have a drink. That tea was horrible!'
sentences.translation: لكن عودوا إلى الفندق ولنشرب شيئاً. كان ذلك الشاي مروعاً!

sentences.text: As we were having our drinks, Franklin Clarke said, 'I suppose we can guess what you're trying to do. You're trying to prove that Cust's alibi is false.'
sentences.translation: بينما كنا نشرب، قال فرانكلين كلارك:

sentences.text: You seem very pleased, but I don't know why. You haven't got a new fact of any kind.'
sentences.translation: تبدو سعيداً جداً، لكنني لا أعرف لماذا. لم تحصل على حقيقة جديدة من أي نوع.

sentences.text: 'No - that is true,' said Poirot. Then he continued, 'My friend Hastings told me once that he had, as a young man, played a game called The Truth.'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو. ثم تابع:

sentences.text: Everyone was asked three questions. They had to promise to answer two questions truthfully. He paused. 'Eh bien, I want to play that game.'
sentences.translation: كان يُسأل كل شخص ثلاثة أسئلة. كان عليهم أن يوعدوا بالإجابة على سؤالين بصدق. توقف.

sentences.text: But one will be enough. One question to each of you.'
sentences.translation: لكن سؤال واحد سيكون كافياً. سؤال واحد لكل واحد منكم.

sentences.text: 'Of course,' said Clarke impatiently. 'We'll answer anything.'
sentences.translation: قال كلارك بنفاد صبر.

sentences.text: 'Ah, but I want it to be more serious than that. Do you all promise to speak the truth?'
Everyone became as serious as Poirot. They all promised. Then Poirot turned to Franklin Clarke.
sentences.translation: أصبح الجميع جادين مثل بوارو. وعد الجميع. ثم التفت بوارو إلى فرانكلين كلارك.

sentences.text: 'What did you think of the hats that the ladies wore at Ascot this year?'
Franklin Clarke stared at him in surprise.
sentences.translation: حدق فرانكلين كلارك فيه بدهشة.

sentences.text: 'Is this a joke?'
'Certainly not.'

Clarke began to smile. 'Well, Monsieur Poirot, I didn't actually go to Ascot, but I saw some of the women driving to the races and their hats this year were an even bigger joke than the hats they usually wear.'
sentences.translation: بدأ كلارك يبتسم.

sentences.text: Poirot smiled and turned to Donald Fraser.
sentences.translation: ابتسم بوارو والتفت إلى دونالد فريزر.

sentences.text: 'When did you take your holiday this year?'
Fraser stared. 'My holiday? The first two weeks in August.'
sentences.translation: حدق فريزر.

sentences.text: Then Poirot turned to Thora Grey and I heard a slight change in his voice. His question came sharp and clear.
sentences.translation: ثم التفت بوارو إلى ثورا غراي وسمعت تغيراً طفيفاً في صوته. جاء سؤاله حاداً وواضحاً.

sentences.text: 'Mademoiselle, after Lady Clarke's death, did you hope to marry Sir Carmichael?'
The girl jumped up. 'How dare you ask me such a question! It's insulting!'
sentences.translation: قفزت الفتاة.

sentences.text: 'Perhaps. But you have promised to speak the truth. Yes or no?'
'Sir Carmichael was wonderfully kind to me. He treated me almost like a daughter. And that's how I felt to him - I was fond of him, and grateful, too.'
'Excuse me, but that is not answering yes or no, mademoiselle.'
'The answer, of course, is no!'
He turned to Megan Barnard. The girl's face was very pale.
sentences.translation: التفت إلى ميغان بارنارد. كان وجه الفتاة شاحباً جداً.

sentences.text: 'Mademoiselle, what do you hope will be the result of my questions? Do you want me to find out the truth or not?'
Megan's head went back proudly. 'No!' she said clearly.
sentences.translation: ارتفع رأس ميغان بفخر.
قالت بوضوح.

sentences.text: We all jumped. Poirot sat forward, studying her face.
sentences.translation: قفزنا جميعاً. جلس بوارو إلى الأمام، دارساً وجهها.

sentences.text: 'Mademoiselle Megan,' he said, 'you may not want the truth but - you can speak it!' he said.
sentences.translation: قال،
قال.

sentences.text: He turned towards the door, then remembered Mary Drower.
sentences.translation: التفت نحو الباب، ثم تذكر ماري دراور.

sentences.text: 'Tell me, have you a young man?'
Mary looked at him nervously 'Oh, Mr Poirot. I - I - well, I'm not sure.'
sentences.translation: نظرت إليه ماري بتوتر:

sentences.text: Poirot smiled. Then he looked round for me.
sentences.translation: ابتسم بوارو. ثم نظر حوله بحثاً عني.

sentences.text: 'Come, Hastings, we must start for Eastbourne.'
The car was waiting and soon we were driving along the coast road that leads through Pevensey to Eastbourne.
sentences.translation: كانت السيارة تنتظر وسرعان ما كنا نقود على طول الطريق الساحلي الذي يؤدي عبر بيفنزي إلى إيستبورن.

sentences.text: Poirot seemed very pleased with himself. As we passed through Pevensey, he suggested that we should stop and look at the castle there.
sentences.translation: بدا بوارو سعيداً جداً بنفسه. وبينما كنا نمر عبر بيفنزي، اقترح أن نتوقف وننظر إلى القلعة هناك.

sentences.text: As we were returning to the car, we passed a group of children in a circle singing a song.
sentences.translation: بينما كنا عائدين إلى السيارة، مررنا بمجموعة من الأطفال في دائرة يغنون أغنية.

sentences.text: 'What is it that they are saying, Hastings?' asked Poirot.
sentences.translation: سأل بوارو.

sentences.text: I listened until I understood.
sentences.translation: استمعت حتى فهمت.

sentences.text: 'And catch a fox
And put him in a box
sentences.translation: ووضعه في صندوق

sentences.text: And never let him go.'
sentences.translation: وعدم تركه يذهب أبداً.

sentences.text: Poirot repeated the words. His face suddenly became very serious.
sentences.translation: ردد بوارو الكلمات. أصبح وجهه فجأة جاداً جداً.

sentences.text: 'That is very terrible, Hastings.' He was silent. 'You hunt the fox here?'
sentences.translation: كان صامتاً.

sentences.text: 'I don't. I've never been able to afford to hunt. And I don't think there's much hunting in this part of the world.'
'I meant in England generally. A strange sport. The dogs run after the fox and at last they catch him and he dies - quickly and horribly.'
But the quick, cruel death is better than what those children were singing... It is not good to be shut away - in a box - for ever...
sentences.translation: لكن الموت السريع القاسي أفضل من ما كان هؤلاء الأطفال يغنونه... ليس جيداً أن تُحبس بعيداً - في صندوق - إلى الأبد...

sentences.text: Tomorrow, I am going to visit Cust Now let's go back to London.'
sentences.translation: غداً، سأزور كاست. الآن لنعد إلى لندن.

sentences.text: 'Aren't we going to Eastbourne?' I cried.
sentences.translation: صرخت.

sentences.text: 'What for? I know quite enough now'
I was not present at the interview between Poirot and that strange man, Alexander Bonaparte Cust.
sentences.translation: لم أكن حاضراً في المقابلة بين بوارو وذلك الرجل الغريب، ألكسندر بونابرت كاست.

sentences.text: Because of his relationship with the police, Poirot was able to be there, but I wasn't included in the special permission that was needed.
sentences.translation: بسبب علاقته بالشرطة، تمكن بوارو من التواجد هناك، لكنني لم أُدرج في الإذن الخاص الذي كان مطلوباً.

sentences.text: Poirot also wanted the interview to be completely private - the two men face to face. But when Poirot came back, he told me all about it in great detail.
sentences.translation: أراد بوارو أيضاً أن تكون المقابلة خاصة تماماً - الرجلان وجهاً لوجه. لكن عندما عاد بوارو، أخبرني بكل شيء بالتفصيل.

sentences.text: Mr Cust seemed smaller, and to stoop even more. His fingers pulled nervously at his coat. For a time, Poirot sat and looked at him.
sentences.translation: بدا السيد كاست أصغر، وأكثر انحناءً. أصابعه شدت معطفه بتوتر. لبعض الوقت، جلس بوارو ونظر إليه.

sentences.text: At last he said gently, 'Do you know who I am?'
sentences.translation: أخيراً قال بلطف:

sentences.text: Mr Cust shook his head. 'No - no, I don't. Or are you from Mr Maynard - from his law office?'
sentences.translation: هز السيد كاست رأسه.

sentences.text: He was polite, but didn't seem very interested. His mind seemed to be on something else, something inside himself.
sentences.translation: كان مهذباً، لكنه لم يبدُ مهتماً جداً. بدا عقله مشغولاً بشيء آخر، شيء داخله.

sentences.text: 'I am Hercule Poirot...'
He said the words very gently... and watched for the effect. Mr Cust lifted his head a little.
sentences.translation: قال الكلمات بلطف شديد... وراقب التأثير. رفع السيد كاست رأسه قليلاً.

sentences.text: 'Oh yes?' he said. Then, a minute later, he repeated the words again. 'Oh yes?' This time he sounded different - more interested. He looked at Poirot.
sentences.translation: قال. ثم، بعد دقيقة، كرر الكلمات مرة أخرى.
هذه المرة بدا مختلفاً - أكثر اهتماماً. نظر إلى بوارو.

sentences.text: Poirot looked back and nodded.
sentences.translation: نظر بوارو إليه وأومأ.

sentences.text: 'Yes,' he said. 'I am the man that you wrote the letters to.'
sentences.translation: قال.

sentences.text: At once, the contact was broken. Mr Cust dropped his eyes and spoke crossly.
sentences.translation: فوراً، انقطع الاتصال. أنزل السيد كاست عينيه وتحدث بغضب.

sentences.text: 'I never wrote to you,' he said. 'Those letters weren't written by me. I've said so again and again.'
sentences.translation: قال.

sentences.text: 'I know,' said Poirot. But if you did not write them, who did?'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: 'An enemy. I must have an enemy. They are all against me. The police - everyone - all against me.'
Poirot didn't reply.
sentences.translation: لم يرد بوارو.

sentences.text: Everyone has been against me - always.'
sentences.translation: الجميع كان ضدي - دائماً.

sentences.text: 'Even when you were a child?'
Mr Cust seemed to think about that.
sentences.translation: بدا السيد كاست يفكر في ذلك.

sentences.text: 'No - no - not exactly then. My mother was very fond of me. She thought I was going to be special - that I could do anything.' He was silent for a minute.
sentences.translation: صمت دقيقة.

sentences.text: 'But she was quite wrong. I was afraid of people. I had a bad time at school. And later when I smarted work, I had the feeling that everyone thought I was stupid.'
'And in the war? asked Poirot.
sentences.translation: سأل بوارو.

sentences.text: 'You know,' said Mr Cust, and his face lit up, 'I enjoyed the war. I felt, for the first time, like a man.'
sentences.translation: قال السيد كاست، وأضاء وجهه،

sentences.text: His smile disappeared. 'But then I got hit on the head, so they made me leave the army. I started working in an office, but things were very difficult. I had very little money.'
sentences.translation: اختفى ابتسامته.

sentences.text: And then I got the offer of the job selling stockings.'
sentences.translation: وبعد ذلك حصلت على عرض العمل في بيع الجوارب.

sentences.text: 'You told us the name of the company. But you know now, don't you,' said Poirot in a gentle voice, 'that that company didn't employ you?'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو بصوت لطيف،

sentences.text: 'That's because they're against me too. I've got their letters to me, giving me instructions about places to go to, and a list of people to visit.'
'Their letters weren't written,' said Poirot. 'They were typed. All those letters were typed on the machine which was found in your room.'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: So it seems that you typed them yourself and, posted them to yourself?'
sentences.translation: لذا يبدو أنك طبعتها بنفسك، وأرسلتها إلى نفسك؟

sentences.text: 'No, no!' said Mr Cust. 'It because they're all against me.'
sentences.translation: قال السيد كاست.

sentences.text: 'And the ABCs that were found in the cupboard?'
'I know nothing about them. I thought they were stockings.'
'Why did you put a mark by the name of Mrs Ascher in that first list of people in Andover?'
Because I decided to visit her first. One must begin somewhere. But I didn't murder her! I'm completely innocent. It's all a mistake.'
sentences.translation: لأنني قررت زيارتها أولاً. على المرء أن يبدأ من مكان ما. لكنني لم أقتلها! أنا بريء تماماً. كلها غلطة.

sentences.text: Look at that second crime - the Bexhill one. I was playing cards in Eastbourne.'
sentences.translation: انظر إلى الجريمة الثانية - جريمة بيكسهيل. كنت ألعب الورق في إيستبورن.

sentences.text: 'You play cards very well, I believe,' said Poirot.
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: 'I - I, well, I believe I do. You'd be surprised how a game of cards can bring strangers together.'
I remember one man - I've never forgotten him because of something he told me. We just got talking over a cup of coffee, and we started playing cards'
sentences.translation: أتذكر رجلاً - لم أنسه أبداً بسبب شيء أخبرني به. بدأنا نتحدث فقط على فنجان قهوة، وبدأنا نلعب الورق.

sentences.text: 'What did he tell you? asked Poirot.
sentences.translation: سأل بوارو.

sentences.text: Mr Cust's is face looked worried.
sentences.translation: بدا وجه السيد كاست قلقاً.

sentences.text: 'He read my future in my hand. He said I would be one of the most famous men in England before I died.'
He said the whole country would talk about me. But he said - he said - I would die a violent death.' He was silent suddenly.
sentences.translation: قال إن كل البلاد ستتحدث عني. لكنه قال - قال - إنني سأموت موتاً عنيفاً.

sentences.text: My head... I suffer very badly... I get cruel headaches sometimes. And then there are times when I don't know...'
sentences.translation: رأسي... أعاني بشدة... أصاب بصداع قاسٍ أحياناً. وهناك أوقات لا أعرف فيها...

sentences.text: He stopped.
sentences.translation: توقف.

sentences.text: 'But you do know, don't you,' Poirot said, 'that you carried out the murders!'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو،

sentences.text: Mr Cust looked up. He looked strangely at peace.
sentences.translation: رفع السيد كاست رأسه. بدا مسالماً بشكل غريب.

sentences.text: 'Yes,' he said. 'I know.'
sentences.translation: قال.

sentences.text: 'But - I am right, am I not? You don't know why you carried them out?'
Mr Cust shook his head.
sentences.translation: هز السيد كاست رأسه.

sentences.text: 'No he said. 'I don't.'
sentences.translation: قال.

sentences.text: CHAPTER TWELVE
sentences.translation: الفصل الثاني عشر

sentences.text: Poirot Explains
sentences.translation: بوارو يشرح

sentences.text: Poirot called a meeting of the Special Legion.
sentences.translation: دعا بوارو إلى اجتماع للفيلق الخاص.

sentences.text: 'From the beginning,' he said, 'I have been worried about the why of this case. The mystery was not the mystery of the murders, but the mystery of A B C.'
sentences.translation: قال،

sentences.text: Why was it necessary for him to carry out these murders? Why did he choose me as his enemy?
sentences.translation: لماذا كان من الضروري له أن ينفذ جرائم القتل هذه؟ لماذا اختارني عدواً له؟

sentences.text: 'It is no answer to say that the man was mad. As soon as I received the first letter, I was upset and worried.'
It seemed to me that there was something very wrong about the letter.'
sentences.translation: بدا لي أن هناك شيئاً خاطئاً جداً في الرسالة.

sentences.text: 'You were quite right,' said Franklin Clarke.
sentences.translation: قال فرانكلين كلارك.

sentences.text: 'Yes. But then, at the beginning, I made a serious mistake. The letter made me very worried. The police thought it was a joke.'
I was sure that a murder would happen in Andover. As you know, a murder did happen.
sentences.translation: كنت متأكداً أن جريمة قتل ستحدث في أندوفر. كما تعلمون، حدثت جريمة قتل.

sentences.text: 'There was no way of knowing who the person was who had carried out the murder. I had to try and understand what kind of a person had done it.'
I had to discover the motive of the crime, the motive of the letter.
sentences.translation: كان عليّ اكتشاف دافع الجريمة، ودافع الرسالة.

sentences.text: 'Why did the murderer send the letter to me? Why not to Scotland Yard, or to a newspaper? Why to Hercule Poirot? Was it for a personal reason?'
Then the second letter arrived - and was followed by the murder of Betty Barnard. It became clear now that the murders were going to take place according to an alphabetical plan.
sentences.translation: ثم وصلت الرسالة الثانية - وتلاها جريمة قتل بيتي بارنارد. أصبح واضحاً الآن أن جرائم القتل ستحدث وفقاً لخطة أبجدية.

sentences.text: But why did ABC need to carry out these murders?
sentences.translation: لكن لماذا احتاج ABC إلى تنفيذ جرائم القتل هذه؟

sentences.text: 'When we think about the four victims - or three of them (since I know very little about Mr Downes or Mr Earlsfield) - we realise that it was possible for the murderer to kill them without anyone suspecting him.'
The clear suspects were Franz Ascher, Donald Fraser or Megan Barnard, or possibly Mr Clarke.
sentences.translation: كان المشتبه بهم الواضحون هم فرانز آشر، ودونالد فريزر، أو ميغان بارنارد، أو ربما السيد كلارك.

sentences.text: Why, then, did the murderer need to call attention to himself? Why did he need to leave on each body an ABC railway guide?
sentences.translation: لماذا، إذن، احتاج القاتل إلى لفت الانتباه إلى نفسه؟ لماذا احتاج إلى ترك دليل سكك حديدية ABC على كل جثة؟

sentences.text: 'I was learning certain things about the murderer. His crimes were listed alphabetically - that was clearly important.'
His victims were men and women, and of different ages. So age and sex were not important to him.
sentences.translation: كان ضحاياه رجالاً ونساءً، ومن أعمار مختلفة. لذا لم يكن العمر والجنس مهمين بالنسبة له.

sentences.text: 'The choice of the ABC suggested to me that it was someone who was interested in railways. This is more common in men than in women.'
Small boys love trains more than small girls. It might be a sign, too, of someone whose mind was not of an adult - someone who was still a 'boy'.
sentences.translation: الأولاد الصغار يحبون القطارات أكثر من البنات الصغيرات. قد تكون علامة أيضاً على شخص لم يكن عقله عقل شخص بالغ - شخص كان لا يزال 'صبياً'.

sentences.text: 'The death of Betty Barnard gave me other clues. She was strangled with her own belt - therefore she was killed by someone she was friendly with'
Betty Barnard liked attention from good-looking men. She went out with A B C, so he was attractive to women.'
sentences.translation: أحبت بيتي بارنارد اهتمام الرجال الوسيمين. خرجت مع A B C، لذا كان جذاباً للنساء.

sentences.text: Donald Fraser jumped up angrily. 'Mr Poirot - please.'
sentences.translation: قفز دونالد فريزر غاضباً.

sentences.text: 'It's finished' said Poirot. 'I will say no more. We will pass to the next murder, the murder of Sir Carmichael Clarke.'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: Here the murderer goes back to his first method - hitting the victim on the head. We were unlucky over this crime since the warning letter did not reach us in time.
sentences.translation: هنا يعود القاتل إلى طريقته الأولى - ضرب الضحية على الرأس. كنا غير محظوظين بهذه الجريمة لأن رسالة التحذير لم تصل إلينا في الوقت المناسب.

sentences.text: Therefore no preparations could be made to stop the crime.
sentences.translation: لذلك لم يكن من الممكن اتخاذ أي استعدادات لإيقاف الجريمة.

sentences.text: 'Then the clue of the stockings was discovered. The appearance of a stocking- seller near the scene of each crime could not be a coincidence.'
So he must be the murderer. But his description, as given by Miss Grey, did not match my picture of the man who strangled Miss Barnard.
sentences.translation: لذا لا بد أنه القاتل. لكن وصفه، كما قدمته الآنسة غراي، لم يتطابق مع صورتي للرجل الذي خنق الآنسة بارنارد.

sentences.text: A fourth murder was carried out - the murder of a man named George Earlsfield - in mistake, we thought, for a man named Downes.
sentences.translation: نُفذت جريمة قتل رابعة - جريمة قتل رجل يُدعى جورج إيرلسفيلد - بالخطأ، كما اعتقدنا، بدلاً من رجل يُدعى داونز.

sentences.text: And now the murderer's luck changes and A B C is at last arrested. The case, as Hastings says, has ended! The man is in prison. Finish!
sentences.translation: والآن يتغير حظ القاتل ويُقبض على A B C أخيراً. القضية، كما يقول هاستينغز، قد انتهت! الرجل في السجن. انتهى!

sentences.text: 'But not for me! I still don't know the why! And there is one small annoying fact. The man Cust has an alibi for the night of the Bexhill crime'
'That's been worrying me, too, said Franklin Clarke.
sentences.translation: قال فرانكلين كلارك.

sentences.text: 'Yes,' continued Poirot. 'The alibi seems real. But it cannot be real unless... and now we come to two very interesting ideas.'
sentences.translation: تابع بوارو.

sentences.text: Supposing, my friends, that while Cust was responsible for three of the crimes - the A, C and D crimes - he did not carry out the B crime!'
sentences.translation: لنفترض، يا أصدقائي، أنه بينما كان كاست مسؤولاً عن ثلاث من الجرائم - جرائم A و C و D - فإنه لم ينفذ جريمة B!

sentences.text: 'Monsieur Poirot. It isn't -' said Megan Barnard. Poirot silenced Megan Barnard with a look.
sentences.translation: قالت ميغان بارنارد. أسكت بوارو ميغان بارنارد بنظرة.

sentences.text: 'Be quiet, mademoiselle,' said Poirot. 'I want the truth! I have finished with lies. Suppose, I say, that someone else murdered Betty Barnard.'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: 'Monsieur Poirot! Surely all the crimes were done by the same person!'
Poirot took no notice of Megan and continued, 'I told you that there was a second idea. Supposing that someone else killed Betty Barnard? Did that someone else do the other murders, too?'
sentences.translation: لم يعر بوارو اهتماماً لميغان وتابع:

sentences.text: 'But that doesn't make sense!' cried Clarke.
sentences.translation: صرخ كلارك.

sentences.text: 'Doesn't it? I examined the letters again. I had felt from the beginning that there was something wrong with them. I had thought they were written by a madman.'
But then I realised - they were not. They were false. The writer was only pretending to be mad.
sentences.translation: لكنني أدركت بعد ذلك - أنها لم تكن كذلك. كانت مزيفة. كان الكاتب يتظاهر فقط بالجنون.

sentences.text: 'What would be the reason for writing such letters? To call the police's attention to the murders!'
At first, it did not seem to make sense. And then I saw light. It was to call the police's attention to several murders - to a group of murders, so that one of those murders would not be noticed!
sentences.translation: في البداية، لم يبدُ الأمر منطقياً. ثم رأيت النور. كان الهدف جذب انتباه الشرطة إلى عدة جرائم قتل - إلى مجموعة من جرائم القتل، بحيث لا تُلاحظ إحدى تلك الجرائم!

sentences.text: 'I was facing a very clever murderer. Not Mr Cust! I was facing a very different kind of man - a man who enjoyed behaving like a boy (remember the schoolboy- like letters and the railway guide) and who was attractive to women.'
A man who played an important part in one of the crimes!
sentences.translation: رجل لعب دوراً مهماً في إحدى الجرائم!

sentences.text: 'I thought about all the crimes again. The Andover crime? The most likely suspect was Franz Ascher, but I could not imagine that Ascher could invent and carry out such a complicated plan.'
The Bexhill crime? Donald Fraser was clever and had ability, but his motive for killing his girlfriend could only be jealousy. It was very unlikely that such a crime would be planned.
sentences.translation: جريمة بيكسهيل؟ كان دونالد فريزر ذكياً ولديه قدرة، لكن دافعه لقتل صديقته لا يمكن أن يكون سوى الغيرة. كان من غير المحتمل جداً أن تكون جريمة كهذه مخططة.

sentences.text: 'We now come to the Churston crime. Sir Carmichael Clarke was a very rich man. Who will get his money after he dies?'
His wife, who is dying, and then it goes to his brother, Franklin.'
sentences.translation: زوجته، التي تحتضر، ثم تذهب إلى شقيقه، فرانكلين.

sentences.text: Poirot turned slowly round and looked at Franklin Clarke.
sentences.translation: استدار بوارو ببطء ونظر إلى فرانكلين كلارك.

sentences.text: 'I was quite sure then. ABC' and Franklin Clarke were the same person!'
Franklin Clarke is attractive to women - he could easily make a girl in a cafe go out with him. He enjoys making lists - he made a list here one day.
sentences.translation: فرانكلين كلارك جذاب للنساء - يمكنه بسهولة إقناع فتاة في مقهى بالخروج معه. يستمتع بعمل القوائم - لقد وضع قائمة هنا ذات يوم.

sentences.text: And finally, his boyish behaviour - Lady Clarke told us about that. I was quite sure in my own mind. The writer of the letters and the murderer was Franklin Clarke.'
sentences.translation: وأخيراً، سلوكه الصبياني - أخبرتنا الليدي كلارك عن ذلك. كنت متأكداً تماماً في عقلي. كاتب الرسائل والقاتل كان فرانكلين كلارك.

sentences.text: Franklin Clarke started to laugh.
sentences.translation: بدأ فرانكلين كلارك يضحك.

sentences.text: 'And what about our friend Cust? What about the blood on his coat? And the knife he hid? He may say he didn't do the crimes -'
'You are quite wrong,' said Poirot. 'He says he did do the murders. He believes himself to be guilty.'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: But as soon as I saw him, I knew he could not be guilty. He is not clever enough. No, there were two people who played a part in these crimes.
sentences.translation: لكن بمجرد أن رأيته، عرفت أنه لا يمكن أن يكون مذنباً. إنه ليس ذكياً بما يكفي. لا، كان هناك شخصان لعبا دوراً في هذه الجرائم.

sentences.text: The real murderer - clever and daring - and the false murderer - weak and stupid.
sentences.translation: القاتل الحقيقي - الذكي والجريء - والقاتل المزيف - الضعيف والغبي.

sentences.text: 'I think you had the idea when you first met Mr Cust in a coffee shop. You were thinking about murdering your brother.'

You showed me a letter your brother had written to you. In it he showed how fond he was of Miss Thora Grey. You were afraid that when Lady Clarke died, your brother might marry Miss Grey and have children.
sentences.translation: أريتني رسالة كتبها إليك أخوك. أظهر فيها مدى تعلقه بالآنسة ثورا غراي. كنت خائفاً من أنه عندما تموت الليدي كلارك، قد يتزوج أخوك الآنسة غراي وينجب أطفالاً.

sentences.text: Then you would not get any of his money.
sentences.translation: عندها لن تحصل على أي من أمواله.

sentences.text: Your meeting with Mr Cust gave you an idea. His strange names, his epilepsy and his weak character made him the tool that you were looking for. The whole alphabetical plan jumped into your mind.
sentences.translation: لقاؤك بالسيد كاست أعطاك فكرة. أسماؤه الغريبة، وصرعه، وشخصيته الضعيفة جعلته الأداة التي كنت تبحث عنها. قفزت الخطة الأبجدية بأكملها إلى ذهنك.

sentences.text: You contacted a company that made stockings and asked for a large number of stockings to be sent to Cust.
sentences.translation: اتصلت بشركة تصنع الجوارب وطلبت إرسال عدد كبير من الجوارب إلى كاست.

sentences.text: You sent him a number of ABC railway guides. You wrote a letter to him, pretending that it came from the stocking company and offering him good pay for selling stockings.
sentences.translation: أرسلت إليه عدداً من أدلة سكك حديدية ABC. كتبت له رسالة، متظاهراً أنها من شركة الجوارب وعارضاً عليه أجراً جيداً مقابل بيع الجوارب.

sentences.text: You made your plans so well that you typed all the letters that were sent later. Then you gave him the machine on which they were typed.
sentences.translation: وضعت خططك جيداً لدرجة أنك طبعت كل الرسائل التي أُرسلت لاحقاً. ثم أعطيته الآلة التي كُتبت عليها.

sentences.text: 'You found two victims whose names began with A and B. You sent a list of customers in the Andover area to Cust, telling him to go there on a certain date. Mrs Ascher's name was on the list.'
You sent the first ABC letter to me. Then you went to Andover and killed Mrs Ascher. For the second murder, you probably killed Betty Barnard before midnight on the 24th.
sentences.translation: أرسلت رسالة ABC الأولى إليّ. ثم ذهبت إلى أندوفر وقتلت السيدة آشر. بالنسبة للجريمة الثانية، من المحتمل أنك قتلت بيتي بارنارد قبل منتصف ليل الرابع والعشرين.

sentences.text: 'We now come to murder number 3 - the important murder for you. And here I must thank Hastings. He suggested that the third letter was sent to the wrong address on purpose.'
And he was right... I had wondered... why were the letters addressed to Hercule Poirot, a private detective, and not to the police?
sentences.translation: وكان على حق... كنت قد تساءلت... لماذا كانت الرسائل موجهة إلى هرقل بوارو، محقق خاص، وليس إلى الشرطة؟

sentences.text: You wanted one of the letters to get lost and reach us too late. But a letter to Scotland Yard could not get lost. So you sent it to a private address.
sentences.translation: أردت أن تضيع إحدى الرسائل وتصلنا متأخرة جداً. لكن رسالة إلى سكوتلاند يارد لا يمكن أن تضيع. لذا أرسلتها إلى عنوان خاص.

sentences.text: You wanted the police to find out about it only when the murder was safely done.
sentences.translation: أردت أن تكتشف الشرطة الأمر فقط عندما تكون الجريمة قد تمت بأمان.

sentences.text: Your brother's nightly walk gave you the opportunity. And everyone was thinking about ABC. Nobody thought that you might be guilty.
sentences.translation: نزهة أخيك الليلية أعطتك الفرصة. وكان الجميع يفكرون في ABC. لم يفكر أحد في أنك قد تكون مذنباً.

sentences.text: 'After your brother's murder, your purpose was finished. You wanted Mr Cust to be arrested as the murderer, but nobody had noticed him.'
So you decided that one more murder was necessary. You chose Doncaster as the scene of your next crime. Everything was made very public in the newspapers.
sentences.translation: لذا قررت أن جريمة قتل أخرى ضرورية. اخترت دونكاستر كمسرح لجريمتك التالية. تم جعل كل شيء علنياً جداً في الصحف.

sentences.text: 'You gave instructions to Mr Cust to go to Doncaster. In the afternoon he went to a cinema. You were there, too.'
You stabbed a man and put the ABC railway guide under his feet. When Mr Cust left, you followed him and put the bloody knife in his coat pocket.
sentences.translation: طعنت رجلاً ووضعت دليل سكك حديدية ABC تحت قدميه. عندما غادر السيد كاست، تبعته ووضعت السكين الملطخ بالدم في جيب معطفه.

sentences.text: 'And now, my friends, let us imagine how Mr Cust thought about all this. The Andover crime means nothing to him.'
He is shocked and surprised by the Bexhill crime - he was there at about the same time! Then comes the Churston crime. Three crimes and he has been at the scene of each of them.
sentences.translation: إنه مصدوم ومندهش من جريمة بيكسهيل - كان هناك في نفس الوقت تقريباً! ثم تأتي جريمة تشيرستون. ثلاث جرائم وقد كان في مسرح كل منها.

sentences.text: Epilepsy sufferers cannot always remember what they have done... Then he receives the order to go to Doncaster.
sentences.translation: مصابو الصرع لا يستطيعون دائماً تذكر ما فعلوه... ثم يتلقى الأمر بالذهاب إلى دونكاستر.

sentences.text: Doncaster! And the next ABC crime will be in Doncaster. He becomes afraid and tells people he is going to Cheltenham. He goes to Doncaster and visits a cinema in the afternoon.
sentences.translation: دونكاستر! وجريمة ABC التالية ستكون في دونكاستر. يصيبه الخوف ويخبر الناس أنه ذاهب إلى شلتنهام. يذهب إلى دونكاستر ويزور سينما بعد الظهر.

sentences.text: When he gets back to his hotel, he discovers there is blood on his coat.
