sentences.translation: عندما يعود إلى فندقه، يكتشف أن هناك دماً على معطفه.

sentences.text: 'So he thinks - he - he himself is the killer! He is quite sure of the truth - he, Alexander Bonaparte Cust, is a mad killer. He behaves like a hunted animal.'
He goes back to his rented room in London. He has the knife with him still. He hides it behind the coatstand.
sentences.translation: يعود إلى غرفته المستأجرة في لندن. لا يزال معه السكين. يخفيها خلف حاملة المعاطف.

sentences.text: 'Then he is warned that the police are coming. They know! I don't know why he went to Andover - maybe he wanted to look at the place of the crime, although he could remember nothing about it.'
He has no money left - he is very tired... he goes to a police station.
sentences.translation: لم يتبق لديه مال - إنه متعب جداً... يذهب إلى مركز شرطة.

sentences.text: 'When I saw him, I knew at once that he was not the murderer and that my name meant nothing to him! I knew that he thought he was the murderer!'
'Your idea,' said Franklin Clarke, 'is completely mad!'
sentences.translation: قال فرانكلين كلارك،

sentences.text: 'No, Mr Clarke. I found the stick which you used in the Andover and Churston murders in a cupboard at Churston. An ordinary stick with a thick handle.'
Two people from the cinema in Doncaster recognised your photograph. Milly Higley, the waitress at Bexhill, remembered you. And you left a fingerprint on Cust's typewriter.'
sentences.translation: تعرف شخصان من السينما في دونكاستر على صورتك. تذكرتك ميلي هيغلي، النادلة في بيكسهيل. وتركت بصمة إصبع على آلة كاست الكاتبة.

sentences.text: Clarke sat silently for a minute. Then he said, 'You win, Monsieur Poirot!'
sentences.translation: جلس كلارك صامتاً لدقيقة. ثم قال:

sentences.text: He took a small gun out of his pocket and held it to his head. He tried to shoot it, but the gun didn't work. Clarke stared at it in surprise.
sentences.translation: أخرج مسدساً صغيراً من جيبه ووضعه على رأسه. حاول إطلاق النار، لكن المسدس لم يعمل. حدق كلارك فيه بدهشة.

sentences.text: 'No, Mr Clarke,' said Poirot. 'Perhaps you noticed that I had a new servant today - a friend of mine. He used to be a clever thief.'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: He removed your gun from your pocket and made it safe. Then he put it back. No, Mr Clarke, there will be no easy death for you. Your crime was not at all English - not fair.'
sentences.translation: أزال مسدسك من جيبك وجعله آمناً. ثم أعاده. لا يا سيد كلارك، لن يكون هناك موت سهل لك. كانت جريمتك غير إنجليزية على الإطلاق - غير عادلة.

sentences.text: Two detectives from Scotland Yard came out from the next room. One of them was Crome. They arrested Franklin Clarke and took him away.
sentences.translation: خرج محققان من سكوتلاند يارد من الغرفة المجاورة. كان أحدهما كروم. اعتقلا فرانكلين كلارك وأخذاه بعيداً.

sentences.text: As the door behind Franklin Clarke closed, I am sorry to say that I started to laugh. Poirot looked at me in surprise.
sentences.translation: عندما أُغلق الباب خلف فرانكلين كلارك، يؤسفني أن أقول إنني بدأت أضحك. نظر إليّ بوارو بدهشة.

sentences.text: 'It's because you told him his crime wasn't fair,' I said.
sentences.translation: قلت.

sentences.text: 'It was quite true. It was very cruel - not only the murder of his brother, but to shut a man away for ever in a prison for mad people. Like a living death.'
To catch a fox and put him in a box and never let him go! That is not sport - not fair.'
sentences.translation: الإمساك بثعلب ووضعه في صندوق وعدم تركه يذهب أبداً! هذه ليست رياضة - ليست عادلة.

sentences.text: Megan Barnard said, 'I can't believe it - I can't. Is it true?'
sentences.translation: قالت ميغان بارنارد:

sentences.text: 'Yes, mademoiselle,' said Poirot. 'It's finished.'
sentences.translation: قال بوارو.

sentences.text: He turned to Fraser. 'Mademoiselle Megan was always afraid that you were responsible for the second crime.'
sentences.translation: التفت إلى فريزر.

sentences.text: 'I thought so myself at one time,' said Donald Fraser quietly.
sentences.translation: قال دونالد فريزر بهدوء.

sentences.text: 'Because of your dream? Your dream has a very natural explanation. In it you find that one sister is being replaced by the other.'
Mademoiselle Megan is taking the place of her sister in your heart. But you feel guilty so you try to kill the thought.
sentences.translation: الآنسة ميغان تأخذ مكان أختها في قلبك. لكنك تشعر بالذنب فتحاول قتل الفكرة.

sentences.text: Do not be afraid to forget,' said Poirot gently. 'Mademoiselle Megan is very special. She has a wonderful heart.'
sentences.translation: لا تخف من النسيان،
الآنسة ميغان مميزة جداً. لديها قلب رائع.

sentences.text: Donald Fraser's eyes lit up. 'I believe you're right,' he said.
sentences.translation: أضاءت عينا دونالد فريزر.
قال.

sentences.text: We all crowded round Poirot, asking questions.
sentences.translation: تجمّعنا جميعاً حول بوارو، نطرح الأسئلة.

sentences.text: 'Why did you ask us those truth questions, Poirot?'
'I wanted to see Franklin Clarke's face when I asked my question of Mademoiselle Thora. His eyes were full of hate and anger.'
'It's because you told him his crime wasn't fair,' I said.
sentences.translation: قلت.

sentences.text: 'It was quite true. It was very cruel - not only the murder of his brother, but to shut a man away for ever in a prison for mad people. Like a living death.'
To catch a fox and put him in a box and never let him go! That is not sport - not fair.'

sentences.translation: الآنسة ميغان تأخذ مكان أختها في قلبك. لكنك تشعر بالذنب فتحاول قتل الفكرة.

sentences.text: Do not be afraid to forget,' said Poirot gently. 'Mademoiselle Megan is very special. She has a wonderful heart.'
sentences.translation: لا تخف من النسيان،
الآنسة ميغان مميزة جداً. لديها قلب رائع.

sentences.text: Donald Fraser's eyes lit up. 'I believe you're right,' he said.
sentences.translation: أضاءت عينا دونالد فريزر.
قال.

sentences.text: We all crowded round Poirot, asking questions.
sentences.translation: تجمّعنا جميعاً حول بوارو، نطرح الأسئلة.

sentences.text: 'Why did you ask us those truth questions, Poirot?'
'I wanted to see Franklin Clarke's face when I asked my question of Mademoiselle Thora. His eyes were full of hate and anger.'
'It's because you told him his crime wasn't fair,' I said.
sentences.translation: قلت.

sentences.text: 'It was quite true. It was very cruel - not only the murder of his brother, but to shut a man away for ever in a prison for mad people. Like a living death.'
To catch a fox and put him in a box and never let him go! That is not sport - not fair.'
sentences.translation: الإمساك بثعلب ووضعه في صندوق وعدم تركه يذهب أبداً! هذه ليست رياضة - ليست عادلة.

We all crowded round Poirot, asking questions.
sentences.translation: تجمّعنا جميعاً حول بوارو، نطرح الأسئلة.

sentences.text: 'Why did you ask us those truth questions, Poirot?'
sentences.translation: "لماذا سألتنا أسئلة الحقيقة تلك يا بوارو؟"

sentences.text: 'I wanted to see Franklin Clarke's face when I asked my question of Mademoiselle Thora. His eyes were full of hate and anger.'
sentences.translation: "أردت رؤية وجه فرانكلين كلارك عندما طرحت سؤالي على الآنسة ثورا. كانت عيناه مليئتين بالكراهية والغضب."

sentences.text: Poirot turned to me.
sentences.translation: التفت بوارو إليّ.

sentences.text: 'You remember, Hastings, the old story about catching a fox and putting him in a box and never letting him go?'
sentences.translation: "أتذكر يا هاستينغز، القصة القديمة عن الإمساك بثعلب ووضعه في صندوق وعدم تركه يذهب أبداً؟"

sentences.text: 'Yes,' I said. 'But what has that to do with Franklin Clarke?'
sentences.translation: "نعم،" قلت. "لكن ما علاقة ذلك بفرانكلين كلارك؟"

sentences.text: 'It has everything to do with him,' said Poirot gravely.
sentences.translation: "له علاقة بكل شيء به،" قال بوارو بجدية.

sentences.text: 'When I heard the children singing that song at Pevensey, I understood everything. To catch a fox and put him in a box and never let him go - that is what Franklin Clarke tried to do with Mr Cust.'
sentences.translation: "عندما سمعت الأطفال يغنون تلك الأغنية في بيفنزي، فهمت كل شيء. الإمساك بثعلب ووضعه في صندوق وعدم تركه يذهب أبداً - هذا ما حاول فرانكلين كلارك فعله بالسيد كاست."

sentences.text: He shut him away forever in a prison for mad people. Like a living death. That is very cruel - not fair.'
sentences.translation: حبسه إلى الأبد في سجن للمجانين. مثل موت حي. هذا قاسٍ جداً - غير عادل."

sentences.text: 'It was quite true,' said Megan Barnard quietly. 'It was very cruel.'
sentences.translation: "كان ذلك صحيحاً تماماً،" قالت ميغان بارنارد بهدوء. "كان قاسياً جداً."

sentences.text: 'Yes,' said Poirot. 'It was very cruel - not only the murder of his brother, but to shut an innocent man away for ever in a prison for mad people.'
sentences.translation: "نعم،" قال بوارو. "كان قاسياً جداً - ليس فقط قتل أخيه، بل حبس رجل بريء إلى الأبد في سجن للمجانين."

sentences.text: A few days later we had a visit from Mr Alexander Bonaparte Cust.
sentences.translation: بعد بضعة أيام، تلقينا زيارة من السيد ألكسندر بونابرت كاست.

sentences.text: He shook Poirot's hand and said, 'Do you know, a newspaper has actually offered me a hundred pounds if I tell them about my life. I - I - really don't know what to do about it.'
sentences.translation: صافح يد بوارو وقال: "أتعلم، عرضت عليّ إحدى الصحف فعلاً مائة جنيه إذا أخبرتهم عن حياتي. أنا - أنا - حقاً لا أعرف ماذا أفعل بشأن ذلك."

sentences.text: 'You should not accept a hundred,' said Poirot. 'Say that five hundred is your price. And tell the other newspapers about it as well.'
sentences.translation: "لا يجب أن تقبل مائة،" قال بوارو. "قل إن خمسمائة هو سعرك. وأخبر الصحف الأخرى بذلك أيضاً."

sentences.text: You must realise that you are a very famous man. Probably the most famous man in England.'
sentences.translation: يجب أن تدرك أنك رجل مشهور جداً. ربما أشهر رجل في إنجلترا."

sentences.text: Mr Cust looked very happy.
sentences.translation: بدا السيد كاست سعيداً جداً.

sentences.text: 'Do you know, I believe you're right, Monsieur Poirot,' said Mr Cust.
sentences.translation: "أتعلم، أعتقد أنك على حق يا سيد بوارو،" قال السيد كاست.

sentences.text: 'The money will be nice - very nice. I'll have a little holiday... And then I want to give a nice wedding present to Lily Marbury - really a dear girl.'
sentences.translation: "سيكون المال لطيفاً - لطيفاً جداً. سآخذ عطلة صغيرة... ثم أريد تقديم هدية زفاف لطيفة لليلي ماربوري - فتاة عزيزة حقاً."

sentences.text: 'You are quite right,' said Poirot. And - just a word - what about a visit to an eye doctor? The reason for those headaches is probably that you need new glasses.'
sentences.translation: "أنت على حق تماماً،" قال بوارو. "و - كلمة واحدة فقط - ماذا عن زيارة طبيب عيون؟ السبب وراء تلك الصداعات هو على الأرجح أنك بحاجة إلى نظارة جديدة."

sentences.text: 'Do you think so?' Mr Cust shook him warmly by the hand. 'You're a very great man, Monsieur Poirot.'
sentences.translation: "هل تعتقد ذلك؟" صافحه السيد كاست بحرارة. "أنت رجل عظيم جداً يا سيد بوارو."

sentences.text: When Mr Cust had left, my old friend smiled across at me.
sentences.translation: عندما غادر السيد كاست، ابتسم صديقي القديم لي.

sentences.text: 'So, Hastings, we went hunting once more, did we not?'
sentences.translation: "إذن يا هاستينغز، ذهبنا للصيد مرة أخرى، أليس كذلك؟"
